boundaries.statement: Each Mathematics block has a concise probe capable of revealing existing understanding of the intended learning, not only its prerequisites. Use independent task-specific evidence; vocal or fast responses alone do not establish mastery. One task may check both prerequisite and intended learning when it genuinely exposes both.

For each substantial task identify its added mathematical demand or justified practice purpose. Do not allocate a long block to recording solutions already established. Permit independent transfer using established concepts; do not require a demonstrated copy of every problem-solving pathway.

Each block provides executable conditional support, normal-teaching and advancement routes with task IDs/final slide destinations and explicit skip points. Students demonstrating the opening learning independently can proceed to substantial prepared mathematics. Mixed readiness uses independent evidence and concurrent tasks; supported success requires an independent recheck.

Task substance and estimated duration are plausible for the available time including immediate understanding. Prepared advancement tasks include hints and exact answers or valid-solution criteria and remain connected to the central idea. Exit evidence uses an aligned fresh application without introducing a new concept. Headings, slide count and busywork do not establish sufficiency.

release_rule: Every scheduled Mathematics instance needs explicit PASS evidence for every applicable boundary. A missing result, NA or FAIL blocks whole-pack release. Structural validity alone is not pedagogical acceptance.
